To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adrenal hormones and a daily feeding rhythm are indispensable to maintain daily rhythms of metabolic/adipokines and clock genes in epididymall white adipose tissue, respectively.

the feeding rhythm is necessary for maintaining the daily gene expression rhythms of the metabolic and adipokine genes in the epididymal WAT, but not for maintaining the daily rhythms of clock genes in this tissue.
the adrenal hormones and feeding are indispensable for maintaining rhythmic expression of metabolic genes, but not of clock genes, in rat epididimal white adipose tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control peripheral circadian rhythms and their importance in the regulation of energy metabolism.
the role of the adrenal hormones and feeding in the synchronization of peripheral tissue clocks.
the mechanisms that maintain the peripheral clocks in the absence of the master SCN clock.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the daily feeding rhythm, but not adrenalectomy, can be a sufficient Zeitgeber for maintaining the clock gene rhythms in the eWAT, whereas both are necessary to sustain the rhythmic expression of metabolic/adipokines.
adrenal hormones, feeding rhythm and the SCN are indispensable for maintaining clock gene and rhythmic metabolic/adipo‐kin gene expression in eWAD.

both adrenal hormones and the feeding rhythm are indispensable signals in the maintenance of daily rhythms of eWAT metabolic/adipokines, whereas adrenal hormones are sufficient for the maintenance of daily clock gene rhythms in eWAT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adrenal hormones, feeding rhythm and the SCN are indispensable for maintaining clock gene and metabolic/adipokines gene rhythms in eWAT.

adrenal hormone rhythm is a more important signal than feeding rhythm for maintenance of daily rhythms in clock genes, while the opposite is true for the maintenance of daily rhythms of metabolic/adipokines in eWAT.

the daily feeding rhythm and adrenal hormones, which are the most likely signals from SCN, are both necessary for the maintenance of daily rhythms in metabolic and adipokine genes in eWAT, but that adrenal hormones alone are sufficient to maintain clock gene rhythms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the peripheral clock in eWAT is more sensitive to disruption of the feeding rhythm than the SCN clock.
the feeding rhythm is a strong synchronizer for eWAT metabolic/adipokines, whereas the SCN is a strong synchronizing signal for eWAT clocks.
the feeding rhythm, in combination with the adrenal hormones, is an essential component of the peripheral clocks, which are synchronized by the master SCN clock.
